question: Should Gateway support scheme-level browser-origin wildcards such as `chrome-extension://*`, and if yes should that live inside `allowedOrigins` or in a dedicated constrained pattern setting?
rationale: This changes which browser-origin WebSocket and trusted-proxy HTTP requests can pass Gateway authorization, so automation should not choose the wildcard grammar or security posture on its own.

options.title: Define Constrained Pattern Contract
options.body: Add a reviewed pattern grammar, docs, audit handling, and allow/reject tests for approved extension/custom-scheme cases before implementation.

options.title: Keep Exact Origins Only
options.body: Land exact opaque-origin fixes separately and defer or close the changing-extension-ID wildcard request as outside current Gateway policy.

options.title: Allow Chrome Extension Wildcard Only
options.body: Accept `chrome-extension://*` narrowly inside `allowedOrigins`, but require scheme-specific matching and negative security tests rather than generic trailing-prefix matching.

recommendation.title: Define Constrained Pattern Contract
recommendation.body: Add a reviewed pattern grammar, docs, audit handling, and allow/reject tests for approved extension/custom-scheme cases before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and continues to review the Gateway origin-security boundary most directly affected by this decision.
